Features

Controls for speech, text, and pronunciation.

Eloqium gives you separate controls for the sound of the voice and for the way incoming text is prepared for speech. The descriptions below explain what the settings change and how the available choices differ.

Voice

Choose a voice and adjust the way it sounds.

The first two settings categories cover the voice itself and additional voice-character adjustments.

Voices and regional variants

Eloqium currently provides eight regional language variants: US English, UK English, Spanish for Spain, Spanish for Mexico and Latin America, French for France, French for Canada, German, and Italian. Every variant uses the same eight voice presets: Reed, Shelley, Bobby, Rocko, Glen, Sandy, Grandma, Grandpa.

View the complete voice list→

Speech rate

The Speech rate setting uses a relative scale from -10 to +10, with 0 representing the engine’s normal baseline. When Force rate is disabled, Eloqium uses the speech-rate value supplied by the Android application making the request. When it is enabled, the configured Eloqium value is used instead. Unlock maximum rate extends the upper limit available to the forced rate setting.

Pitch

The Pitch setting provides a relative adjustment from -10 to +10 around the selected voice’s base pitch. With Force pitch disabled, Eloqium follows the pitch requested through Android’s TTS interface; with it enabled, Eloqium applies the configured pitch value instead.

Volume

Force volume enables a relative digital gain adjustment on the synthesized 16-bit PCM audio before it is supplied to Android. The Volume setting can attenuate the signal below its baseline or increase it above the baseline, with the resulting samples constrained to the 16-bit range. This does not replace Android’s normal system playback volume control.

Voice characteristics

Inflection, Head size, Roughness, and Breathiness provide additional relative controls around the selected voice’s baseline parameters. These settings are separate from the basic rate and pitch controls, so they can be adjusted when you want to change the character of the voice without simply making it faster or higher.

ECI Voice Tags

The ECI Voice Tags setting controls whether compatible inline backquote voice and control annotations in incoming text are allowed through the compatibility-processing stage. It is intended for applications or content that deliberately use such annotations.

Sampling rate

Eloqium provides seven selectable sampling rates: 8,000 Hz, 11,025 Hz, 16,000 Hz, 22,050 Hz, 32,000 Hz, 44,100 Hz, and 48,000 Hz. The default rate is 11,025 Hz. This setting changes the rate used by the native synthesis engine rather than an Android device requirement.

Eloqium foreground service

Provides foreground-service support that can improve reliability during background speech, particularly on devices with restrictive background management. The service includes an ongoing notification while active and access to Android battery optimization settings.

Text processing

Decide how symbols, numbers, and written forms are prepared.

These settings affect the text that is prepared for the native speech synthesizer. They are particularly useful when ordinary written text contains information that you want presented differently when heard aloud.

Punctuation

Enable Process punctuation when you want punctuation marks to be verbalized. The Punctuation level setting determines how broad the spoken-punctuation set is:

None
Punctuation remains part of normal speech phrasing, but Eloqium does not replace punctuation marks with their spoken names.
Some
Eloqium speaks a core group of symbols, including mathematical and structural characters such as #, %, &, +, =, @, and < and >.
Most
The Some set is extended to include brackets, braces, quotation marks, dashes, underscores, colons, and semicolons. Colons in recognized time expressions can also be spoken at this level.
All
The Most set is extended to sentence and clause punctuation such as periods, commas, question marks, and exclamation marks. Decimal and thousands separators can also be verbalized in numeric expressions.
Custom
You enter the characters you want Eloqium to speak. Characters outside that selection continue through the ordinary text-processing path rather than being automatically added to the spoken-punctuation set.

Punctuation that is not spoken can still affect ordinary phrasing and pause behavior. Number and time expressions also receive special handling so that punctuation inside them is not treated in exactly the same way as punctuation standing alone.

Numbers

When Use number processing is enabled, the selected mode determines how a multi-digit sequence is separated before synthesis:

Smart
Selects formatting based on context, preserving dates, times, decimals, currency, and phone numbers while grouping long digit sequences.
Digits
Separates a multi-digit number into individual digits before synthesis. For example, 1984 becomes 1 9 8 4.
Pairs
Groups digits from the left in pairs. For example, 1984 becomes 19 84, while 123 becomes 12 3.
Triplets
Groups digits from the right in groups of three. For example, 1234567 becomes 1 234 567.

Phonetic pronunciation entries are protected from number processing, so digits already contained inside a pronunciation annotation are not reformatted by this setting.

Capital indication

Controls how uppercase letters are handled during speech. The available options are None, Pitch raise, and Say capital. When Pitch raise is selected, Eloqium raises pitch only for standalone uppercase one-letter words, such as A or I, without altering uppercase characters inside ordinary words.

Abbreviations

Use abbreviations enables the built-in abbreviation dictionary. It expands supported forms such as titles, road and address abbreviations, and common expressions including e.g., i.e., and etc.. The processor also applies context-sensitive handling for forms such as St. so that common uses can be distinguished.

Emoji and emoticons

Emoji / Emoticon enables speech descriptions for supported emoji sequences and a defined set of ASCII emoticons. Emoji are converted into localized spoken descriptions before synthesis. The emoticon processor protects patterns that resemble URLs, times, ratios, Windows paths, code operators, and similar text so they are not accidentally treated as emoticons.

Intonation pauses

Intonation pauses changes how Eloqium prepares pauses around punctuation. When enabled, the normal pause-preserving mode is retained. When disabled, the broader pause-processing path is used. Phrase prediction is a separate setting and is enabled by default.

Pronunciation

Customize individual words and phrases.

The User Dictionary can replace incoming text or supply a specific pronunciation for text that needs to be spoken differently. Dictionaries are associated with a regional language and can contain multiple independent rules.

Read the dictionary guide→

Android TTS

Eloqium is implemented as an Android TextToSpeechService. Compatible applications can use Android’s standard text-to-speech interface to request supported languages and voices and to send text for synthesis.
